Gadi Eisenkot has vowed to oust Benjamin Netanyahu, but still has to get enough parties on board

Israel's new parliament has been sworn in, as opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot seeks to oust caretaker Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

The former army chief has been tasked with forming a government after receiving more recommendations from members of the Knesset than Netanyahu, although not all those backing him are willing to govern together.

Eisenkot's bloc of four parties won 48 seats in October's election, while Netanyahu's bloc won 53, leaving both short of a majority in the 120-seat Knesset. He has 28 days to build a coalition, with a possible two-week extension.

Almost half of the new MKs did not serve in the previous parliament, while Arab-led parties have a record number of seats.

Shortly after they were sworn in, Netanyahu and Eisenkot warned parliament about the perils of supporting a government led by the other.

"[And] to those who are thinking of establishing a government that includes supporters of terror and haters of Israel, or that will be dependent on them, I ask you, are you prepared to be dependent on those whose goal is the destruction of the Jewish state?" said Netanyahu, alluding to the prospect of an Eisenkot-led government reliant on support from Arab parties.

He also appealed for the formation of a government of national unity as the only way to confront what he said was the threat of "a nuclear Iran".

Eisenkot sharply criticised Netanyahu's comments.

"I sat and listened to the outgoing prime minister's delusional, divisive, hate-filled and shameful speech, exploiting a state occasion," he said. "I am now even more convinced that he is unfit to remain in office for even one more minute."

The outcome of the election, which was widely seen as a referendum on Netanyahu, means there is a period of uncertainty over who will form the next government. Netanyahu will remain caretaker prime minister until then - a process which could take from days to months.

One of the most dramatic results was the performance of Israel's two Arab-led alliances - the United Arab List and the Joint List - which won an unprecedented 19 seats between them following a surge in turnout among Arab voters.

The Arab parties could therefore hold the balance of power, although Netanyahu has ruled out governing with them and three of the parties in Eisenkot's bloc have opposed including them in a coalition.

On Sunday, President Isaac Herzog tasked Eisenkot with trying to form a government.

Speaking at the president's residence, the centrist Yashar party leader called for the formation of a "national emergency government" - an implicit appeal to parties to put ideological differences aside to remove Netanyahu from office.

This, he said, would "require creative and unconventional political steps".

Eisenkot said any party or MK prepared to accept four principles could join his proposed government. Those are recognition of Israel as a Jewish and democratic state; accepting the values of the Declaration of Independence; backing mandatory military, national or civilian service for all, including communities currently exempt; and recognising Hamas as a terrorist organisation and committing to dismantling its military and governing capabilities.

The four requirements, however, could present significant obstacles to Eisenkot's potential partners.

The conscription of ultra-Orthodox Jewish men, who are exempt from military service if they are in full-time religious study, was a major election issue.

The ultra-Orthodox United Torah Judaism (UTJ) and Shas parties, which won 13 seats in total, have fiercely objected to attempts to change the status quo - something that all parties in Eisenkot's bloc campaigned to do.

Eisenkot's four principles are also contentious for the Arab parties. Both emphasise equal national and civic rights for Israel's Arab citizens, who form about 20% of the population; the vast majority of Israeli Arabs are not required to serve in the military; and neither has publicly recognised Hamas as a terrorist organisation.

The Arab parties could, though, help Eisenkot form a minority government. The United Arab List, which won eight seats, has said it is willing to be part of an Eisenkot-led coalition, while the Joint List, which won 11 seats, has offered parliamentary support from the outside.

If Eisenkot accepted such an arrangement, he would still have to persuade other parties in his bloc to agree. Avigdor Lieberman, whose Yisrael Beiteinu party won seven seats, has so far refused to join a minority government dependent on Arab MKs.

In return for their support, the ultra-Orthodox parties would be likely to demand major concessions on military conscription, which might be unacceptable to most of the parties in Eisenkot's bloc.

The Metropolitan Police have said several people contacted them during the trial and following the conviction and sentencing of the disgraced comedian Russell Brand, "to provide information or report a potential criminal allegation".

Speaking to BBC Breakfast, Det Supt Andy Furphy, who led the Brand investigation, said officers were "looking at exactly what we've got" and "whether they're information that points to behaviour or whether they could constitute a criminal offence".

On Monday, Brand was sentenced to 10 years and six months in prison, after being convicted of rape and sexual assault.

In his sentencing remarks, judge Joel Bennathan described him as a "sexual predator" and criticised his "staggering arrogance".

The 51-year-old was sentenced to nine years for rape, with an additional 18 months, nine months and eight months for three counts of sexual assault. The latter sentences are to run concurrently.

He was found guilty of the charges involving four women between 2004 and 2009.

"We know that he had used his following [online] to try and cow people into silence," added Dame Caroline.

"And the fact that they [the women] were able to come forward and tell their story and tell their truth and secure this conviction because of it is unbelievably impressive."

Sales of essential goods such as bottled water and canned food soared in the 10 days following the launch of the government's "Be Ready" emergency preparedness campaign on 22 October, research indicates.

Hand sanitiser sales were up 83%, sales of bottled water rose 67% and tinned and jarred goods climbed 37%, according to data from retail research firm Worldpanel by Numerator.

The government's public awareness campaign encouraged people to stock up in case of disruption to essential services by severe weather or cyberattacks.

However, Worldpanel said that while households were stockpiling essentials, they were not panic buying.

The government campaign encouraged people to keep three days-worth of food and water in their homes.

Wet wipes, a torch and cash were also recommended.

After the campaign launch, the equivalent of an extra 400,000 people per day bought tinned meat, Worldpanel said, although the typical amount remained at 500g, which suggests a gradual stocking-up.

"Shoppers clearly took notice of the 'Be Ready' campaign, but this wasn't panic buying, with less than a third of households buying bottled water in October," said Fraser McKevitt, head of retail and consumer insight at Worldpanel by Numerator.

"Growth came from more people adding the recommended items on the government's checklist to their weekly shop, not from shoppers piling their trolleys high, which is very much in line with what the government wanted households to do," he said.

Sales of tinned and jarred goods rose from £58.2m in the 10 days to 2 November 2025 to £79.5m over the same period in 2026.

Bottled water sales jumped from £13.6m to £22.8m compared with a year earlier and hand sanitiser sales climbed from £497,000 to £908,000.

Further evidence of stockpiling came from food firm Princes on Tuesday, which said demand for tinned tuna, meat and vegetables had risen following the government's campaign.

Princes interim chief executive Giuseppe Mastrolia said the jump in demand "further reinforces the relevance of our core categories in providing affordable, nutritious and convenient food solutions".

The "Be Ready" campaign warns that severe weather and cyber attacks could disrupt essential services, and British households need to make sure they have what they need - for example, bottled water, and long-life food that doesn't need to be kept in the fridge such as dried fruit and nuts.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has said everyone should have "those supplies in the house to get you through those moments".

Disaster recovery expert Lucy Easthope previously told the BBC that the UK was playing "massive catch up" to other European nations in terms of preparedness.

These include France, Germany Denmark, Sweden, and Norway.

A number of experts have been calling for the UK to put more emphasis on food security, with some arguing that the government itself should take responsibility for food stockpiling, rather than individual households.

In October, a group of more than 180 experts signed an open letter , external to Burnham and first secretary of state Louise Haigh calling for local authorities to have a duty to prevent and respond to food supply emergencies.

They pointed out that a government survey found that 29% of people in the UK could not afford to keep a few days worth of food in the house.

Stockpiles of blood have dropped below required levels due to falling donor numbers

An amber alert has come into force for the first time as stocks of blood in Scotland have dropped to unprecedented low levels due to the shortage of donors.

The warning has been sent to hospitals across the country by the Scottish National Blood Transfusion Service (SNBTS), urging medical staff to only use Type O blood when essential.

Type O blood is particularly important for transfusions as O-negative acts as a universal donor and O-positive is the most common blood type in the UK, with about 35% of the population having it.

Stocks have consistently been below target levels for several weeks and Group O blood has fallen to below two days of reserves on several occasions recently.

SNBTS aims to always retain 5 – 7 days supply of all blood groups.

The alert comes after a decline in people joining the blood donation register.

In the past decade SNBTS said there had been a 24% drop in blood donors - about 30,000 people.

The blood transfusion service said it was particularly struggling to attract younger donors.

Hospitals are estimated to need about 135,000 units of blood each year to treat patients.

The SNBTS said that to do this appointments at its five national donor centres in Aberdeen, Dundee, Edinburgh, Glasgow and Inverness needed to be fully booked all year round.

However, an average of just 85% of these appointment slots are filled.

Debbie McNaughton, director of donor and transport services at the SNBTS, told Radio Scotland Breakfast that currently, about 2% of Scotland's population are signed up to give blood, with the majority donating once a year.

"If they could be donating maybe twice or three times a year, that would hugely help to provide resilience for the blood supply," she said.

McNaughton went on to urge anyone who is healthy and 17 or over to sign up to the donor register.

The amber alert will trigger new protocols in hospitals to minimise non-essential usage of O-type blood, but emergency operations, blood transfusions, transplants and cancer surgeries will continue as normal.

The alert has initially been issued for an initial period of 4-6 weeks but will be kept under close review.

MN202611_1mo84i2vc6g.t:
This was during Kigali Protocol meeting last week

KIGALI — As world leaders and climate negotiators gather in Türkiye for COP31, the United Kingdom is putting its climate partnership with Rwanda in the spotlight, highlighting projects ranging from sustainable cooling to wetland restoration and climate finance.

The British High Commission in Rwanda has been engaged in online coverage of the partnership in recent weeks, using videos, photographs and other content to showcase practical projects supported by the UK.

Much of the attention has focused on the 10th anniversary of the Kigali Amendment to the Montreal Protocol and the 38th Meeting of the Parties to the Montreal Protocol, held in Kigali earlier this month.

The UK has highlighted the Africa Centre of Excellence for Sustainable Cooling and Cold Chain, known as ACES, as one of the clearest examples of what the Kigali Amendment can deliver in practice.

The centre is a UK-funded partnership with the Rwandan government that focuses on cleaner and more efficient cooling and cold-chain systems.

Cooling is becoming increasingly important as temperatures rise and demand for refrigeration and air conditioning grows.

But conventional cooling equipment can consume large amounts of energy and rely on refrigerants with high global warming potential.

The Kigali Amendment, agreed in Rwanda in 2016, seeks to phase down hydrofluorocarbons, or HFCs, powerful greenhouse gases widely used in cooling equipment.

The UK has described ACES as a model for how countries can combine climate action with practical economic and development needs.

The centre works on training technicians, certifying equipment and developing cold-chain systems that can support farmers, food producers and health services.

Its work also addresses post-harvest losses and the need to maintain reliable temperatures for products such as vaccines.

The British High Commission’s recent posts have coincided with two major international climate moments.

MOP38 in Kigali marked 10 years since the adoption of the Kigali Amendment.

The meeting also focused heavily on the financing required to help developing countries implement the agreement.

The Multilateral Fund is estimated to require between $1.23 billion and $1.69 billion for the 2027–2029 period.

The UK has used the anniversary to underline the importance of financing countries that are being asked to move towards cleaner cooling technologies.

In one video posted from MOP38, a UK climate official explained the history of the Montreal Protocol and the evolution of the Kigali Amendment, while highlighting Rwanda’s role in sustainable cooling through ACES.

Another post described ACES as a “shining example” of sustainable cooling innovation.

The UK and Rwanda, together with Brazil, are also co-champions of the Friends of the Kigali Amendment initiative, which seeks greater ambition and implementation of the agreement.

The focus is increasingly shifting from agreeing climate targets to making those targets work on the ground.

The UK mission has also used more accessible demonstrations to explain the challenge.

On November 9, Development Director Billy Stewart appeared in a video at ACES, pedalling a bicycle-powered cooling system.

The demonstration was designed to show how much energy can be required to produce something as simple as a cold drink.

As demand for cooling expands, countries need systems that consume less energy and use refrigerants with lower environmental impacts.

For Rwanda, the issue has implications well beyond air conditioning.

Reliable cooling is essential for agriculture, food storage, transport, health services and other parts of the economy.

The UK sees ACES as a regional hub that can help Rwanda and other African countries develop the skills and systems needed to meet that demand.

The centre has also been involved in partnerships with Rwanda’s Ministry of Agriculture, including work on rehabilitating cold rooms and expanding sustainable cold-chain systems.

The British High Commission’s recent climate messaging has also extended beyond cooling.

On November 9, UK officials visited Nyandungu Eco Park in Kigali to highlight the connection between climate action and nature restoration.

The restored wetland is home to hundreds of bird species and has received support through UK climate and nature finance.

The visit was timed with the opening of COP31 and was used to illustrate the importance of restoring ecosystems while building more resilient cities and communities.

The UK has also supported programmes designed to improve access to weather and climate information, allowing communities to prepare earlier for floods, droughts and other climate-related shocks.

These projects form part of a broader partnership focused on helping Rwanda mobilise finance for green growth and climate resilience.

Rwanda is particularly vulnerable to floods, landslides and droughts, which can damage infrastructure, agriculture and livelihoods.

The UK has therefore focused part of its support on strengthening institutions, developing projects that can attract investment and creating mechanisms that can bring public and private capital into climate action.

This includes work involving the Rwanda Green Fund, blended finance, green bonds and carbon markets.

The current focus builds on a broader UK-Rwanda climate partnership.

In March, Kigali hosted a UK-Rwanda Climate Partnership Conference under the theme “Catalysing Green Investment in Africa”.

The conference brought together experts and policymakers around the challenge of turning climate commitments into investable projects.

About £20 million in UK investment has been linked to climate-resilient systems and initiatives including ACES.

The British High Commission is also recruiting a Climate Programme, Policy and Partnership Manager in Kigali to work on climate finance, resilience and green growth.

The position, advertised in late October, is part of the mission’s Growth, Climate and Human Capital Group.

The recruitment underlines that the partnership is not limited to individual projects.

It is also aimed at building institutional capacity to manage climate finance and develop longer-term cooperation.

The UK government’s recent messaging presents Rwanda as more than a recipient of climate support.

It presents the country as a place where climate solutions can be developed, tested and potentially scaled across Africa.

The sustainable cooling initiative connects the Kigali Amendment’s global climate objective with everyday issues such as food security, healthcare and energy use.

Nature restoration projects such as Nyandungu add another dimension, linking climate resilience with urban development and biodiversity.

As COP31 gets underway, the UK is using these examples to make a broader point: climate commitments matter most when they produce practical changes in people’s lives.

For Rwanda, the partnership provides access to finance, technology and expertise.

For the UK, it offers an opportunity to demonstrate how international climate cooperation can move from pledges to projects.

And for both countries, the challenge is increasingly about scale — ensuring that initiatives developed in Rwanda can reach more communities and contribute to the wider African response to a warming planet.

Israeli forces carried out a raid in the Old City of Nablus, near Burqa, on Sunday

Israeli forces have shot dead a 14-year-old Palestinian boy during an operation in the occupied West Bank, Palestinian officials say.

Moataz Daghlas was killed on Monday evening in the village of Burqa, north-west of Nablus, according to the Palestinian health ministry.

The Israeli military said soldiers identified "several terrorists who intended to hurl stones" in an area where stones had previously been thrown at Israeli vehicles. The soldiers fired towards them "to remove the threat", it added.

The Palestinian Red Crescent said its teams treated two people with gunshot wounds, but that Israeli forces blocked their access to a third wounded person and detained three volunteer paramedics.

Moataz Daghlas's relatives said Israeli authorities were withholding his body.

Meanwhile, Palestinian news agency Wafa identified the two Palestinians wounded during the raid as a 17-year-old child, who it said was shot in the abdomen and pelvis, and a 19-year-old man, who was shot in the hand.

According to the UN, at least 98 Palestinians, including 22 children, have been killed by Israeli forces or settlers in the West Bank since the start of the year.

Six Israelis, both security forces and civilians, have been killed by Palestinians in the West Bank over the same period, it says.

The rules of engagement for Israeli forces were reportedly broadened after the deadly Hamas-led attacks on Israel on 7 October 2023, allowing soldiers increased discretion to use lethal force against a perceived threat.

In June, the UN Human Rights Office in the occupied Palestinian territory said it had verified the killing of 241 Palestinian children by Israeli security forces and settlers in the West Bank since then.

Most of the children were teenage boys and, in many cases, Israeli authorities accused them of having engaged in stone-throwing as justification, it found.

The UN office said its assessment was that none of the children killed while involved in confrontations with Israeli forces had posed an imminent threat to life, which it said was the only legal justification for the use of lethal force in the West Bank under international law.

The United States government has issued restrictions to travellers originating from the DRC not to bord flights to USA if they have been to the central African state 21 days prior.

“Travelers, including Americans, who have been in the DRC within 21 days of their flight will not be allowed to board flights with U.S. destinations,” US embassy in Kinshasa said on Tuesday.

The embassy said ,”travelers should plan to remain outside the United States until at least 21 days after they leave the DRC.”

“This applies even if travelers were on an airplane that stopped at an airport in DRC regardless of whether they disembarked or stayed on the airplane.”

Ku mugoroba wo ku wa mbere ni bwo Jean Léonard Teganya ukekwaho kugira uruhare muri jenoside mu Rwanda yageze i Kigali yoherejwe na Leta Zunze Ubumwe z'Amerika.

Ubushinjacyaha bw'u Rwanda buvuga ko Teganya, w'imyaka 55, akekwaho ibyaha byakorewe mu mujyi wa Butare – ubu ni mu Karere ka Huye – mu majyepfo y'u Rwanda, mu gihe yari umunyeshuri wigaga ubuganga muri Kaminuza y'u Rwanda.

Teganya akekwaho kugira uruhare mu rupfu rw'Abatutsi biciwe hirya no hino mu mujyi wa Butare, harimo no mu bitaro bya Kaminuza bya Butare.

Nta cyo aravuga ku mugaragaro kuri ibyo byaha akekwaho.

Bitandukanye n'abandi bakekwaho jenoside boherejwe mu Rwanda, nta makuru agaragaza ko Teganya yaba yarakatiwe n'inkiko Gacaca.

Teganya yagejejwe mu Rwanda mu masaha y'ijoro ryakeye. Akimara gusohoka mu ndege, yakiriwe yambitswe amapingu. Yagaragaye atuje kandi nta gihunga agaragaza mu maso.

Yari aherekejwe n'abakozi bambaye imyenda iriho ibirango bya polisi y'Amerika, bamushyikiriza polisi y'u Rwanda, mbere yo kuzuza inyandiko zo guhererekanya hagati y'impande zombi.

Ubushinjacyaha buvuga ko Teganya akurikiranyweho ibyaha bivugwa ko yakoze mu gihe yari umunyeshuri wiga ubuganga muri Kaminuza y'u Rwanda aho yakoreraga imyitozo ngiro y'ubuganga.

Umuvugizi w'ubushinjacyaha Faustin Nkusi yavuze ko Teganya akekwaho kwica Abatutsi ubwe, ndetse no kugira uruhare mu gutegura urutonde rw'Abatutsi bagombaga guhigwa no kwicwa.

Nkuko Nkusi yabivuze, Teganya yoherejwe mu Rwanda nyuma y'uko inyandiko zo gusaba ko ashyikirizwa ubutabera zoherejwe muri Amerika mu mwaka wa 2014.

Ubushinjacyaha ntiburatanga ibisobanuro birambuye ku ruhare akekwaho kugira muri jenoside, ariko bumushinja kugira uruhare mu bwicanyi bwakorewe mu mujyi wa Butare no mu nkengero zawo. Akekwaho kandi kugira uruhare mu kurobanura abarwayi b'Abatutsi bari mu bitaro bya Butare aho yakoreraga imyitozo, nyuma bakicwa.

Dosiye ye yitezwe guhera mu rwego rw'igihugu rw'ubugenzacyaha (RIB), kuko nta makuru agaragaza ko yari yaraburanye adahari. Nyuma byitezwe ko izashyikirizwa ubushinjacyaha bufite inshingano zo kumuregera urukiko.

Amakuru avuga ko Teganya yagejejwe mu Rwanda nyuma yo kurangiza igifungo cy'amezi 97 yakatiwe n'urukiko rwo mu mujyi wa Boston muri Amerika, nyuma yo guhamwa n'icyaha cyo kubeshya ku myirondoro ye no guhisha uruhare rwe muri jenoside.

Teganya abaye umuntu wa munani woherejwe n'Amerika mu Rwanda kuva mu mwaka wa 2007.

Teganya yavukiye mu cyahoze ari perefegitura ya Gisenyi, ubu ni mu karere ka Ngororero mu ntara y'uburengerazuba.

Rwanda’s economy expanded by 10.6% in 2025/26, while the country’s foreign exchange reserves reached $2.27 billion, according to the National Bank of Rwanda (BNR) Annual Integrated Report for 2025/26.

The report highlights improvements in economic performance, financial sector stability and access to financial services, alongside developments in inflation, exchange rates and banking sector indicators.

Economic growth increased from 5.7% in 2024/25 to 10.6% in 2025/26, reflecting stronger economic activity during the reporting period.

However, average annual inflation also increased from 5.7% to 9.2%, indicating continued pressure on the cost of goods and services.

The report further shows that the Rwandan franc depreciated by 2.28% against the US dollar during the year, while the country’s international trade deficit narrowed by 2.8%.

Rwanda’s foreign exchange reserves stood at $2,272.79 million, providing an important buffer to support external payments and help the country manage potential economic shocks.

The report also highlights developments in the country’s financial sector, with the central bank’s policy rate increasing from 6.5% in 2024/25 to 8.25% in 2025/26.

Access to credit improved, with the share of adults accessing loans through financial institutions rising from 44% to 48.01%, indicating progress in expanding financial inclusion.

Meanwhile, banks’ capital adequacy ratio increased from 21.6% to 22%, remaining above the minimum regulatory requirement of 15%. This reflects the banking sector’s capacity to absorb potential financial risks.

The ratio of non-performing loans increased slightly from 2.6% to 3%, while the capital adequacy ratio for microfinance institutions declined from 34.7% to 29.8%, although it remained above the regulatory minimum of 15%.

The banking sector’s liquidity ratio also remained strong, although it declined from 289% to 278.7%, still considerably above the minimum requirement of 100%.

The report further provides indicators on Rwanda’s financial markets, including government securities and investment activities, reflecting the central bank’s role in supporting monetary policy implementation and maintaining financial stability.

Through its annual report, BNR provides an overview of its monetary policy decisions, financial sector supervision and other activities aimed at safeguarding the country’s economic stability.

The report serves as an accountability document, helping the public, investors and other stakeholders understand the central bank’s contribution to Rwanda’s economic development and the management of its financial system.

Igihano c'umunyororo w'imyaka 200 caciriwe umuvugabutumwa Paul Mackenzie wo muri Kenya catumye haba abibaza nimba hari ibihano bikaze nk'iki bimaze kubaho, abandi bibaza ku minyororo miremire gusumba iyindi kw'isi imaze gutangwa.

Mackenzie yakatiwe na sentare nkuru y'i Mombasa kubera uruhara rwiwe mu rupfu rw'abantu 191, harimwo abana 190, bapfiriye mw'ishamba rya Shakahola mu ntara ya Kilifi.

Aha turaraba abandi bantu bigeze gukatirwa umunyororo w'imyaka amajana canke ibihumbi.

McLaurin hamwe na mugenziwe Darron Bennalford Anderson bagiriwe n'ivyaha vyo kunyuruza, gufata ku nguvu, no kwiba umukenyezi ageze mu zabukuru.

Uburemere bw'igihano: McLaurin yakatiwe umunyororo usumba uwaciriwe mugenziwe, w'imyaka 21.250.

Ariko rero, haciye imyaka itatu, ico gihano caragabanuweko imyaka 500 inyuma y'uko yunguruje, bituma umunyororo wiwe usigara ku myaka 20.750.

Ku wa 14 Kigarama (12) 1994, Charles Scott Robinson yaragiriwe n'ivyaha bitandatu bijanye no gufata ku nguvu abana, harimwo gufata ku nguvu akoresheje ibindi bintu, gusambanya ku nguvu mu kanwa, hamwe n'ibindi bikorwa vy'agahomerabunwa vyakorewe umwana atarashikana imyaka 16.

Robinson yaciriwe umunyororo w'imyaka 5.000 kuri buri caha muri ivyo bitandatu, bituma umunyororo wiwe wose ushika ku myaka 30.000, ku vyaha vyo gufata ku nguvu no gukorera amabi umwana w'umukobwa yari afise imyaka itatu.

Abacamanza bunganira sentare ni bo bari batanze icipfuzo c'uko kuri buri caha yohabwa umunyororo w'imyaka 5.000, maze umucamanza w'akarere Dan Owens ategeka ko ahabwa ivyo bihano mu rukurikirane (kimwe inyuma y'ikindi).

Intumbero yari iyo kugira ngo Robinson ntaze asubire kurekurwa mu buryo ubwo ari bwo bwose, kuko babona ko "igihano c'ugupfungwa ubuzima bwose ata mahirwe yo kurekurwa atanze ingwati" kitari gikwiye ku vyaha yari yakoze.

Jamal Zougam ni Umunya-Maroc yaciriwe umunyororo kubera uruhara rwiwe mu bitero vy'ibibombe vyagabwe kuri gari ya moshi i Madrid muri Espagne ku wa 11 Ntwarante (3) 2004.

Ivyo bitero vyahitanye abantu 191 vyongera bikomeretsa abarenga 1.800.

Zougam, yari asanzwe akurikiranwa n'inzego z'umutekano kubera isano yari afitaniye n'abanywanyi b'umuhari al-Qaeda, yagirizwa kuba yarateze kimwe muri ivyo bibombe.

Vyongeye yari nyene iduka ryagurishije amaterefone ngendanwa yakoreshejwe mu guturitsa ivyo bibombe.

Mu kwezi kwa Gitugutu (10) 2007, sentare nkuru ya Espagne yamwagirije ivyaha 191 vy'ubwicanyi, rumucira umunyororo w'imyaka 42.922. Ariko rero, azomara mw'ibohero imyaka 40 gusa, kuko ari yo myaka myinshi kuruta iyindi umuntu ashobora gupfungwa hisunzwe amategeko ya Espagne.

Zougam yavukiye i Tangier muri Maroc, hanyuma aja kuba i Madrid muri Espagne.

Ari i Madrid, yari afise iduka ry'amaterefone ngendanwa ryaje kwemezwa ko ryagurishije amaterefone yakoreshejwe mu guturitsa ivyo bibombe ku wa 11 Ntwarante 2004.

Zougam yari yatanguye gukurikiranwa n'inzego z'umutekano muri Mukakaro (7) 2001, inyuma y'aho ubutegetsi bw'Ubufaransa bumenyeshereje ko ashobora kuba yari afitaniye isano n'umurwi wa al-Qaeda muri Espagne.

Mu gikorwa co gusaka inzu yabamwo i Madrid, abajejwe umutekano bahasanze ibikoresho vy'inyigisho z'intambara ishingiye kw'idini rya Islamu, harimwo videwo y'ikiganiro c'uwahoze arongoye al-Qaeda Osama bin Laden, hamwe n'inomero za terefone z'intagondwa zari zizwi ko zifitaniye isano n'uwo murwi.

Othman El Gnaoui ni Umunya-Maroc yaciriwe umunyororo kubera uruhara rwiwe mu bitero vy'ibibombe vyagabwe kuri gari ya moshi i Madrid muri Espagne ku wa 11 Ntwarante (3) 2004, vyahitanye abantu 191 bikanakomeretsa abarenga 1.800.

El Gnaoui, yafatwa nk'uwugira kabiri mu bateguye ivyo bitero inyuma ya Jamal Ahmidan, azwi kandi kw'izina rya "El Chino", yagiriwe n'icaha co gutwara ibiturika vyakoreshejwe muri ico gitero no gutega kimwe muri ivyo bibombe vyaturitse.

Mu kwezi kwa Gitugutu (10) 2007, sentare nkuru ya Espagne yamwagirije ivyaha 191 vy'ubwicanyi, imucira umunyororo w'imyaka 42.924. Ariko rero, azomara mw'ibohero imyaka 40 gusa, kuko ari yo myaka myinshi kuruta iyindi umuntu ashobora gupfungwa hisunzwe amategeko ya Espagne.

El Gnaoui yavukiye i Tétouan muri Maroc, hanyuma aja kuba muri Espagne. Bikavugwa ko yakora akazi k'ubwubatsi imbere y'uko afatwa mu mwaka wa 2004.

Abajejwe umutekano batanguye kumukurikiranira hagufi kubera yikekwa ko yoba yari afise uruhara mu rudandazwa rw'ibiyayuramutwe. Ivyo vyatumye igipolisi gishiraho uburyo bwo kwumviriza ibiyago vya terefone yiwe.

Inyuma yo gusuzuma ibiyago vyafatiwe kuri iyo terefone amaze gufatwa, abakoze amatohoza basanze El Gnaoui yari yaravuganye n'abandi bakekwa gukora iterabwoba hamwe n'abandi bari bagize uruhara muri ayo mabi amayinga makeya imbere y'ivyo bitero vya Madrid.

Bikekwa kandi ko yahuye na Shazad Ali Gutjar, Umunya-Pakistan yari afitaniye ubucuti n'umuhari al-Qaeda yagirizwa uruhara mu gutegura ikindi gitero categerezwa kuba mu gisagara ca Barcelona.

Umunyororo muremure kuruta iyindi yose imaze gutangwa ku caha c'ububeshi wahawe Chamoy Thipyaso hamwe n'abandi indwi bari bafatanije.

Umw'umwe wese yakatiwe umunyororo w'imyaka 141.078 na sentare mpanavyaha y'i Bangkok muri Thaïland ku wa 27 Mukakaro (7) 1989, inyuma yo kwagirwa n'icaha co kunyuruza amafaranga y'abanyagihugu bakoresheje amayeri yo kwegeranya amafaranga yabo ngo babaziganirize, amayeri yarimwo amamiliyoni y'amadolari.

Mu rundi rubanza rwabereye i Palma de Mallorca muri Espagne ku wa 11 Ntwarante 1972, ubushikirizamanza bwasavye ko Gabriel March Grandos, ico gihe yari afise imyaka 22, yokatirwa igihano c'umunyororo w'imyaka 384.912.

Yagirizwa kuba atashikirije amakete 42.768 yari ajejwe gutanga, aho kuri buri kete ubushikirizamanza bwasaba ko yohanwa imyaka icenda y'umunyororo.

Iyi nkuru yateguwe na Martha Saranga, itunganywa na Yusuph Mazimu.

A police officer has died and another has been injured in the northern Spanish city of Oviedo after an explosive device went off at the scene of a shooting.

The blast happened when officers from Spain's canine unit and explosives disposal unit arrived and examined a suspicious backpack following reports of a dispute between neighbours on Tuesday morning .

A woman who had been shot and the injured officer have been taken to hospital for treatment.

The suspect fled the scene and is still at large, police said.

Spanish police paid tribute to the dead officer, who has been named as Juan José, in a statement on X and said: "Our hearts are with his family, friends, colleagues and loved ones."

Officers attended the scene early after receiving reports of an argument between neighbours and upon arriving found a woman who had sustained gunshot wounds, police spokesman Pedro Aguado said.

While searching for the suspected attacker, officers found a suspicious backpack with a flashing light and contacted both the bomb disposal unit and canine unit.

"While the package was being moved outside to ensure the safety of the residents, an explosion occurred," Aguado added.

The explosion left a member of the canine unit dead and an officer from the bomb disposal unit seriously injured, he said.

A three-year-old police dog named Deny was also killed in the explosion.

A widespread police operation is ongoing near the scene of the explosion and officers are continuing to hunt for the suspect.

Taking to social media, Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez said he was "deeply shocked" by the fatal incident and paid tribute to the officer injured in the explosion.

"Your dedication and courage deserve the gratitude of an entire country," he said.

Spanish opposition leader and President of the People's Party Alberto Núñez Feijóo said: "What happened in Oviedo is heartbreaking.

"My condolences to the family of the officer who died and my best wishes for the recovery of the one who was seriously injured.

Mu ngero 10 z’ikawa u Rwanda rwari rwashyize muri aya marushanwa yabereye muri Singapore, esheshatu zahawe ibihembo, zirimo eshatu zahawe Platinum Awards ku manota 90% cyangwa arenga n’izindi eshatu zahawe Gold Awards ku manota ari hagati ya 80% na 89%.

Iki gihembo cya Platinum kivuze ko ikawa igihawe iba igiye ku ikawa nziza yo ku rwego rwa mbere cyangwa “specialty coffee.” Ni mugihe iyahawe Gold Award iba iri ku rwego rwa kabiri muri kawa nziza.

Ibihembo byatanzwe mu nama mpuzamahanga y’ikawa ya ASEAN International Coffee Summit 2026, aho abatunganya n’abacuruza ikawa babonye umwanya wo kumurika umusaruro wabo, guhura n’abaguzi ndetse no gushaka amasoko mashya.

Ikigo cy’Igihugu gishinzwe Iterambere ry’Ubuhinzi n’Ibyoherezwa mu Mahanga (NAEB) kivuga ko iyi ntsinzi igaragaza umusaruro w’imbaraga zimaze igihe zishyirwa mu kuzamura ireme ry’ikawa, kuva ku murima kugeza ku isoko.

Umuyobozi Mukuru wa NAEB, Claude Bizimana, yavuze ko ibihembo u Rwanda rwabonye bigaragaza ko abahinzi, amakoperative, abatunganya ikawa n’abayohereza mu mahanga bakomeje gukora ibishoboka kugira ngo ikawa y’u Rwanda ihangane ku masoko asaba umusaruro mwishi kandi mwiza.

Ati “Kuba twaramenyekanye ku rwego mpuzamahanga nk’uru bigaragaza ireme n’ubushobozi bw’ikawa y’u Rwanda. Ni umusaruro w’imbaraga z’abahinzi, amakoperative, abatunganya ikawa n’abayohereza mu mahanga, kandi bidutera imbaraga zo gukomeza kuzamura ireme, gukurikirana inkomoko y’ikawa no gukomeza kwerekana u Rwanda nk’igihugu gitanga ikawa yihariye kandi ihangana ku isoko mpuzamahanga.”

Abahinzi babonye imbaraga zo gushaka amasoko mashya

Ku bahinzi n’amakoperative, ibihembo byabonetse ni amahirwe yo gukomeza kunoza umusaruro no gushaka amasoko atanga agaciro kanini ku ikawa.

Aimable Nshimiye, uyobora Koperative Abateraninkunga ba Sholi yo mu Karere ka Muhanga, ifite ikawa yahawe igihembo cya Platinum, yavuze ko iki gihembo cyabahaye imbaraga zo gukomeza kuzamura ireme ry’ikawa no kwagura ibikorwa bya koperative.

Ati “Iki gihembo cyongeye kuduha imbaraga zo gukomeza gukora ikawa y’ireme no kwagura ibikorwa bya koperative. Kidufasha kandi kubona amahirwe yo kumenyekanisha ikawa yacu ku masoko mpuzamahanga, bikazagera ku bahinzi binyuze mu kongera amahirwe n’iterambere rya koperative.”

Singapore yabaye umuryango ujya ku isoko rya Aziya

Kwitabira aya marushanwa kandi byahuriranye no gusinya amasezerano y’ubufatanye hagati ya NAEB n’Urugaga rw’Abacuruzi b’Ikawa muri Singapore.

Aya masezerano agamije gukomeza ubufatanye hagati y’inganda z’ikawa z’ibihugu byombi no gufasha ikawa y’u Rwanda kubona umwanya munini ku isoko rya Singapore ndetse n’andi masoko yo mu bihugu bigize ASEAN.

NAEB ivuga ko ibihembo u Rwanda rwabonye bishobora gufasha kongera kumenyekanisha ikawa yarwo ku baguzi mpuzamahanga, abacuruzi, abayitunganya n’abayotsa, cyane cyane ku masoko yo muri Aziya.

U Rwanda rukomeje gushyira imbere kuzamura ireme ry’ikawa no kubona amasoko mashya, kugira ngo kuba ikawa yarwo ikomeje kumenyekana ku rwego mpuzamahanga bihinduke inyungu zifatika ku bahinzi n’abandi bakora muri uru rwego.

Ibi bihembo bije mu gihe u Rwanda rwihaye intego yo kuzamura amafaranga rwinjiza aturutse ku ikawa akagera kuri miliyoni 192 z’amadolari ya Amerika ku mwaka mu 2029.

Imibare ya NAEB igaragaza ko mu mwaka w’ingengo y’imari wa 2025/26, u Rwanda rwohereje mu mahanga toni 23,000 z’ikawa zinjiza miliyoni $139.3, ziyongereyeho 20% ugereranyije na miliyoni zirenga $116 u Rwanda rwinjije mu mwaka wa 2024/25, ubwo rwoherezaga hafi toni 21,000.

Abasirikare bagera kuri 66 ni bo baciriwe igihano co gupfa bagirizwa kuba abanyabwoba, kugarariza no kwanka gukurikiza amategeko bahawe, nk'uko bishikirizwa n'ibimenyeshamakuru vyo muri Repuburika ya Demokarasi ya Kongo (RDC).

Ico gihano caciwe inyuma y'urubanza rw'abasirikare 71 rwabereye mu gisata c'ubutungane ca gisirikare i Walikale, mu ntara ya Kivu ya Ruguru, mu buseruko bwa RDC. Bane muri bo barejejwe, mu gihe uwundi umwe yakatiwe gupfungwa imyaka 10.

Igisirikare ca RDC kivuga ko urwo rubanza rwari rugamije gutsimbataza indero mu basirikare, mu gihe bahanganye n'imirwi yitwaje ibirwanisho mu buseruko bw'ico gihugu.

Ako karere kamaze imyaka mirongo karangwamwo intambara, aho n'ubu ingwano ikibandanya hagati y'ingabo za Reta n'umuhari FRN (Front pour la refondation de la nation), ugizwe n'urunani rw'imihari yitwaje ibirwanisho, harimwo M23.

Amakuru avuga ko abo basirikare bafashwe kw'igenekerezo rya 20 Gitugutu(10) i Walikale, bagirijwe kuba barataye ibirindiro barahunga igihe bariko batana mu mitwe n'abarwanyi ba FRN.

Igikorwa c'igisirikare ca Kongo co guhangana n'imirwi yitwaje ibirwanisho, harimwo M23, kimaze igihe kirekire kigeramiwe n'ukutagira indero ikwiye hamwe n'akajagari mu basirikare.

Reta ya Kongo yagumye yagiriza igihugu kibanyi c'Urwanda gushigikira M23. Ivyo Urwanda ruvyamirira kure, co kimwe na M23, n'ubwo hari ibimenyetso bibigaragaza.

Igisirikare ca Kongo kimaze igihe kinengwa kubera kutagira ubunyamwuga n'akaranga mu kazi, hamwe n'indero bikwiye. Abasirikare na bo bidogera imishahara mito n'ibikoresho bidakwiye.

Mu kwezi guheze, abandi basirikare 27 na bo nyene barakatiwe urwo gupfa, bagirizwa ivyaha bisa n'ivyo. Amakuru avuga ko bari bataye urugamba barahunga igihe bariko batana mu mitwe n'abaroberi.

Muri Ntwarante (3) 2024, RDC yarasubijeho igihano c'urupfu, inyuma y'imyaka 20 cari kimaze gihagaritswe, aho reta yavuze ko ikeneye gutuza "abansi b'igihugu" bari mu gisirikare.

Reta yavuze ko ico gihano kizohabwa kandi abantu bagize uruhara mu mirwi yitwaje ibirwanisho, mu migumuko, hamwe n'abakoze icaha co guhemukira igihugu n'ivyaha vy'intambara.

Kim Kardashian's firm Skims will refund people who bought the advent calendar

Kim Kardashian's Skims is offering customers refunds for its $148 (£110) advent calendar which has been widely criticised on social media.

The accessories advent calendar promised "twelve days of fun surprises" but has been mocked online for the quality of its contents, such as hair clips and keychains, with some comparing them to something you would find down the back of a sofa.

A spokesperson for Skims has told a number of media outlets "for some, the calendar didn't meet expectations" and the company has "personally contacted every customer" to offer a full refund or credit to put towards other products".

The BBC has contacted Skims for comment.

The shapewear and clothing business was co-founded by Kardashian in 2019 and has made the reality TV star a billionaire, according to Forbes magazine.

Skims was valued at $5bn in 2025 when it raised millions of dollars in new funding.

One account on TikTok called spicychathouse compared the contents of the calendar to things "my cat collects from around my house". Another account said it looked like "a bunch of stuff that Kim Kardashian was emptying out of her bedside table".

A number of accounts showed people cleaning out their own sofas and claiming they had accidentally created the Skims advent calendar.

"It is really interesting to see this kind of backlash," said Kate Vlietstra, senior director of food and drink at market research analyst Mintel.

"It is something we have been seeing a bit more in recent years, particularly with the trend for unboxing on social media," she said,

"It means that, inevitably, if people are not feeling they're getting the value that they have hoped for from the advent calendar...they've purchased, then yes, there is going to be a backlash."

Advent calendars remain popular, according to Helen Wing, head of innovation at market research company Ipsos though she said that "the buzz around them has reduced a little bit".

She said according to Ipsos research, people are willing to pay a bit more for an advent calendar but the contents have to justify the price tag.

Using a £285 advent calendar sold by Liberty as an example, Wing said the upmarket department story is "very open about the value of the contents".

"They will say there is over £1,000 worth of content," she said. "If you've got that reassurance when you're making the purchase, particularly if it is for a gift, then it is important to have some faith that the contents are actually going to be worth the money that you're paying."

Arsene Wenger (left) joined Fifa as chief of global football development in 2019

Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger is considering standing against Gianni Infantino as a candidate in Fifa's presidential election.

For weeks, senior figures in European football have been hoping the Frenchman would run for the job, and he is now giving it serious thought.

Wenger is 77, leading to questions over whether he could provide long-term leadership for the sport.

But some of his supporters have told BBC Sport that they would be happy for him to win the election, then stand down before serving a full four-year term.

Infantino's position was plunged into crisis by a backlash caused by his failed plan to sell commercial stakes in the World Cup to private investors.

But he retains support in South America, Africa and Asia, and recently insisted he has the backing of the "vast, vast majority" of world football.

Infantino laughs off resignation questions

However, that support could be tested if Wenger stands.

Fifa's head of global development would have the backing of Uefa, which has spearheaded opposition to Infantino, and he has credibility throughout the footballing world.

Sources close to Wenger say he is yet to decide whether to stand, and they still believe Infantino is favourite to win a fourth and final term in next year's election.

The deadline for candidates to confirm they are standing against Infantino for the election in March is 18 November.

Former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega was the first person to put his name forward in October.

Japan Football Association honorary president Kozo Tashima has also announced his intention to stand.

This month Fifa said "key documents" relating to Infantino's plan to sell stakes in the World Cup would be made available to members of its council, but they will have to travel to its Zurich base, and access will be under "strict protocols".

Last month Uefa gave football's world governing body until 2 November to release details about the controversial Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) proposal, and to answer questions relating to its decision-making.

That followed a council meeting at which Infantino apologised for the abandoned sell-off plot but failed to explain how the proposal was devised, asking that questions be submitted in writing.

Amid the fallout over FFE, Wenger, who has traditionally been loyal to Infantino, distanced himself from the aborted plot.

"I was not involved in this strategic plan and first became aware of the project through media reports," Wenger said at the time.

"The decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question, because I firmly believe in an independent Fifa that serves our game with commitment, transparency and integrity."

Wenger has caused controversy at times in his Fifa role, notably for proposals such as biennial World Cups and a "daylight" offside law.

But he also has a global profile, including in Africa, where Infantino recently received a major re-election boost when receiving the backing of all 54 member national associations after promising an increase in funding.

Known as a champion of African players when in charge at Arsenal, Wenger's support of an expanded 48-team World Cup in order to drive development in countries beyond the game's traditional powers has been well received in the continent.

A community committee has a year to raise £164,000 to purchase Ruscombe Wood

Local villagers are hoping to buy an ancient woodland so it can be saved from private sale and continue to be a sanctuary for generations to come.

Landowners Margaret and David Lloyd have allowed the public to enjoy their 17-acre Ruscombe Wood near Stroud for the last 20 years but have now decided to sell up.

Keen for it to go into the hands of local residents, the couple have given Ruscombe Woodlands Committee one year to raise £164,000 to cover purchase, legal and survey costs.

Martin Humphreys from the committee said: "I like the idea that if we own the woods, nature will become part of the community and we can have that instead of a community hall."

Made up of local residents, the committee have now launched a fundraising campaign to raise the funds for the purchase and said it hopes to protect wildlife and habitat, along with guaranteeing permissive footpaths at the site continue to stay open for everyone.

It also hopes to offer free workshops, including on woodland care, natural skills and creative crafts.

Resident Martin Humphreys said the woodland "has a silent quality"

Margaret, 79, said they had decided it was time to sell their "pretty special piece of ancient woodland" after realising it had become "too much work" for them.

"We want the community to buy it because they all love it and we want it loved like we've loved it all this time," she said.

"Really, we'd like it sold now and we could put it back on the market, but it wouldn't be the same, so the only snag for us is that it wont get done until November 2027," she added.

Margaret said the group also have plans to use the space as a forest school.

Martin said it was "very nice" that the couple had given them time to raise the money needed for the purchase.

He said while the group has to get through a lot of legalities, he likes the idea that the woodland could eventually be owned by everybody.

"It has no public rights of way, it's not been spoilt or overworked, it's wild and has lots of creatures that have made their homes there.

"It has a wonderful silent quality," Humphreys added.

The Congolese army has been fighting rebels for decades

At least 66 soldiers have been sentenced to death in the Democratic Republic of Congo for cowardice, mutiny and refusing to obey orders, local media report.

The sentences followed a trial of 71 soldiers before a military court in Walikale, in North Kivu province, in eastern DR Congo. Four soldiers were acquitted, while another was sentenced to 10 years in prison.

The army said the trial was intended to improve discipline among troops as they battle armed groups in eastern DR Congo.

The region has endured decades of conflict, with fighting continuing between government forces and the Front for the Refoundation of the Nation (FRN), a rebel coalition that includes the M23 group.

The soldiers were reportedly arrested on 20 October in Walikale, where they were accused of abandoning their positions and fleeing during clashes with FRN fighters.

The Congolese army's campaign against armed groups, including the M23, has long been undermined by poor discipline and disorganisation within its ranks.

The government has repeatedly accused neighbouring Rwanda of supporting the M23, an allegation denied by both Kigali and the rebels despite overwhelming evidence.

The army has faced persistent criticism over its lack of professionalism and disciplined, while soldiers have complained of poor pay and inadequate equipment.

Last month, another 27 soldiers were sentenced to death on similar charges of cowardice after reportedly withdrawing from the frontline during clashes with rebels.

In March 2024, DR Congo lifted a 20-year moratorium on the death penalty, citing the need to remove "traitors" within the army.

The government said capital punishment would also apply to people involved in armed groups, insurrection, as well as committing treason and war crimes.

The decision to reinstate the death penalty was widely criticised by rights groups. However, no formal executions have been carried out since the moratorium was lifted.

Since the beginning of 2025, at least 507 soldiers have been convicted, including 381 death sentences, according to figures compiled by French broadcaster RFI.

In October 2025, former Congolese President Joseph Kabila was sentenced to death in absentia on charges including war crimes and treason. He denied the accusations, but did not appear in court to defend himself. He has since been named as the FRN's leader.

Miroslav Klose's FC Nuremberg side sit second in the 2. Bundesliga

It is no surprise Miroslav Klose recognises the value of a true goalscorer.

He is, after all, Germany's all-time leading marksman and until this summer had netted more than any other player in men's World Cup history. Even now, only Kylian Mbappe and Lionel Messi can top his 16 across four tournaments.

But of the more than 300 goals Klose scored in a career that began in Germany's amateur leagues and spanned Kaiserslautern, Werder Bremen, Bayern Munich and Lazio, he reckons all but two came inside the penalty area.

"Thankfully, we've moved away a little from the idea of the false nine or having a second striker playing around the main striker, with everyone coming towards the ball," explains the FC Nuremberg boss.

"For me, the most important thing is that you need someone who is there to score goals. You need someone in the box because that's where you're closest to the goal. That's why I'm a big believer in practising the final ball, whether it's a cross, a shot or something else.

"That's crucial. How do you create that final ball? When you develop automatisms and players get to know each other better, that's when you see harmony on the pitch.

"It can make things look effortless, but it involves a huge amount of work. A lot of work in training and attention to detail, making sure the players communicate with each other and understand their team-mates' strengths and weaknesses."

That focus on detail stems from Klose's diligence during his playing days. He would study opponents' movement, analyse a goalkeeper's position and shape when facing certain shots - do they make themselves big? Are their hands high or low?

"When goals are scored, the whole team deserves credit," adds the 48-year-old, who was as selfless as he was ruthless. "But you still need someone who has that ability in their feet or in their head to put the ball in the net."

"He's a great role model for me" - Former German forward on Harry Kane

Klose was 36 when he won the World Cup with Germany in 2014 - surpassing Ronaldo's goal record in a 7-1 semi-final thrashing of hosts Brazil.

It was the culmination of a career built on hard work after a series of near-misses - something that may offer solace to Harry Kane and England that a major tournament triumph remains possible.

Born in communist Poland, Klose's father Josef - also a footballer, most notably for Auxerre - moved the family to West Germany when his son was eight.

He was never in a big academy, playing in the lower leagues while training as a carpenter before eventually joining Kaiserslautern.

Klose, like Kane, was in his early 20s by the time he established himself in top-flight football, but just two years after his Bundesliga debut was starting a World Cup final defeat by Brazil.

The striker, 38 when he hung up his goalscoring boots, admires the way Kane has evolved as he has matured, using him as an example to his own young prospects.

"You could always see his quality, and he's worked incredibly hard to get where he is," says Klose of the Ballon d'Or winner .

"He's also a great role model for me, particularly because he has stayed in Germany. I often tell my players that they should look at someone like him as an example.

"Young players can't yet have the instinct and experience he has developed, but that's where it starts - thinking about what you can and can't do as a footballer. You have to keep learning. That's the crucial thing for me.

"If you understand that you train to become better, then in five years' time you'll naturally be a different player. But if you think everything will happen automatically just because 10 people around you tell you that you're a fantastic player, I don't think you'll continue to develop."

Klose's Nuremberg have the youngest average age in the 2. Bundesliga

Klose has a knack for working with young talent, previously coaching Bayern Munich's under-17s. His Nuremberg side are the youngest in the German second tier with an average age of 23.3 years, according to Transfermarkt.

"You need that balance and a certain core of experienced players," he explains. "But we're very brave in that respect. Over the three years I've been here, we've made progress in how we assess young players and in the conversations we have about them.

"How do we rate them? How far along are they? What do they need to work on to take the next step? Is it perhaps more about their physical development? Because from a footballing perspective, we're already producing some really good players."

Klose's coaching journey began with the national team before he joined Bayern, briefly becoming Hansi Flick's assistant, and then took his first managerial role at Rheindorf Altach in Austria.

He joined Nuremberg, historically one of Germany's most successful clubs, in 2024 and steered them to 10th and eighth-placed finishes.

This season they sit second, behind Hertha BSC, and are the league's joint-top scorers, with eyes on a return to the Bundesliga for the first time since 2019.

"When I first arrived, I spoke to the youth coaches about the club's DNA and its coaching philosophy, and what they focus on," adds Klose.

"There was already a lot of common ground. We suggested trying certain things because we wanted to do a little more in particular areas, and they were open to that.

"That's important. We benefit from this because our young players are getting opportunities in the first team, and everyone is paying attention to their development.

"But that journey starts with the youth coaches. I know how important it is to take those steps. We're benefiting from that now because we have access to so many young talents.

"As a coaching team, we're brave enough to give them opportunities when we see that they can compete at this level. That's the first step."

Among the 11 to play the most minutes for Klose's side this season, seven are 22 years old or under, including top scorer Mohamed Ali Zoma, already capped by Italy.

"Of course, everyone gets a lot of praise, as is currently the case with Marc Kornwachs," says Klose of a 17-year-old midfielder also catching the eye.

"But his journey isn't over yet. Now it's about helping him become more consistent and establishing himself, while continuing to develop his game and take further steps forward.

"These players are so talented that we have absolutely no hesitation in giving them opportunities, regardless of the scoreline."

Klose was still playing fifth-tier amateur football aged 20 before becoming the World Cup's all-time top goalscorer in 2014

Klose also understands his managerial career is still young - mirroring the humble nature that earned him fair play awards in Germany and Italy.

"I'm very comfortable with the steps I've taken, even though it involves a huge amount of work," he says about his progress. "You learn something every day.

"I've said that I'm already a much better manager than I was three years ago. That's perfectly normal, and you have to embrace it. I've always been willing and eager to learn, and I've always been a hard worker. That isn't going to change."

So what does a Miroslav Klose team look like?

"Personally, as a player, I always liked having the ball for long periods, and that hasn't changed," he explains.

"When you have the ball, you have a certain level of dominance. I know you also have to be very adaptable in terms of possession, and that's something we are. We constantly show the players different ways of playing out of situations.

"It's great to see how they develop and to be able to support individual players along the way. That's exactly the approach I like to take as a manager."

Rwanda National Police has launched a nationwide campaign to help communities prevent fires and respond to them before firefighters arrive, following a series of blazes that have damaged commercial buildings in recent weeks.

The campaign began in November and will run in districts across the country. Training sessions are planned at institutions and busy public places, including bus stations, churches, hotels, markets, garages and large buildings.

Assistant Commissioner of Police Paul Gatambira, head of the Fire and Rescue Brigade, said the campaign would teach people how fires start and spread, how to prevent them and how to use available equipment to respond.

“We want to strengthen cooperation with different groups so we can work together to fight fires,” Gatambira said. “In many cases, information reaches us late. If people nearby had been trained to use fire extinguishers and other equipment, they could take the first steps before we arrive.”

The goal, he said, is to equip residents with the knowledge to act while emergency services are on their way.

Rwanda National Police spokesperson ACP Boniface Rutikanga recently told RBA that firefighters can respond only after a fire has broken out. People at the scene, he said, should take initial steps to contain it, where it is safe to do so, and limit the damage before firefighters arrive.

“We do not want this to be the responsibility of the police alone,” Gatambira said. “We want residents to take part too. In many places, when people see a fire, they act as if it does not concern them and run away.”

Participants will learn about common causes of fires and how to prevent them. The training will also encourage people to use nearby fire-fighting equipment to tackle a blaze when it is safe, rather than simply fleeing.

Police are urging welders to keep fire extinguishers within reach. Developers and managers of commercial buildings, hotels, markets, garages and other busy venues are also being asked to install water supplies and piping that can be used to fight fires. Gatambira said ready access to water is essential, as fetching it from a distant source can cost valuable time during an emergency.

He also called on building managers to check that their fire extinguishers work properly and that enough are available.

The campaign follows several major fires reported in Rwanda since around mid-October. The most destructive was at GOICO market in Muhoza Sector, Musanze District, where goods valued at about Rwf 30 billion were destroyed, according to an assessment. Other recent fires in Kigali damaged factories in the city’s industrial zone.

MN202611_fef7ko841i.t:
The artificial nests are made from woodcrete which is much stronger and more durable than mud

Up to 900 artificial nest "cups" for threatened house martins are set to be installed in Hampshire as part of a conservation project.

The birds migrate from Africa each spring and are on the UK's Red List of endangered bird species. They are thought to have suffered from a lack of wet mud to build nests during the extreme heat in the summer.

Following a pilot project, The Hampshire House Martins Project is offering free cups which save the birds time and energy compared to building their own mud nests.

Project co-ordinator Nigel Matthews encouraged residents, schools and businesses to apply for the free artificial nests "to give these remarkable birds a safe place to raise their young".

Between 1995 and 2024, the UK House Martin population fell by 40%, partly due to poor breeding success.

The birds build distinctive cup-shaped nests beneath the roofs of houses and other buildings, carrying around 1,000 pellets of soft mud to complete each one.

Each April and May, house martins return from Africa to spend the summer in the UK.

The birds often form colonies with several nests in close proximity.

More than 500 nest sites were recorded throughout Hampshire in 2025

The decline in numbers has been blamed on a fall in quantities of insects, as well as hotter, drier weather - as seen during the summer of 2026 - resulting in less wet mud available for nest building.

Modern homes tending to have uPVC soffits also makes it difficult for mud nests to adhere.

Last year the Hampshire Ornithological Society initiative launched a survey, allowing members of the public to record house martin nest locations .

The group is now looking for additional properties where artificial nests will be provided and fitted free of charge - thought to be the biggest such project in the country.

House martin numbers have declined due to hotter, drier weather and a fall in quantities of insects

During the project's pilot, 249 artificial nest cups were installed on buildings close to known nesting sites across northern and eastern Hampshire.

Twenty seven were used by house martins this summer, more than the project team had expected.

Keith Betton, chair of Hampshire Ornithological Society, said: "The response to the first pilot stage of this project showed how strongly people across Hampshire want to help house martins.

"This next phase turns what we have learnt into action by offering hundreds more safe, ready-made nests.

"It gives homeowners, schools and businesses a simple, practical way to support the recovery of this threatened bird."

To quality for a cup, which are provided and installed for free, properties must be within 1km (0.6 miles) of a previously recorded house martin nest.

Host buildings must have suitable overhanging eaves at second story level, between four and seven metres from the ground.

Applications for the nest cups can be made on the Hampshire House Martins Project , external website.

Kimwe mu bibazo nyamukuru impande zompi zidahurizako ni intara ya Donetsk, iri mu buseruko bwa Ukraine, ubu igice kinini cayo kikaba kigenzurwa n'Uburusiya.

Uburusiya busaba Ukraine kurekura ibice ikigenzura vya Donetsk, ariko Ukraine ivyo ntivyerekwa. Ishaka kugumana ivyo bice ahubwo ikipfuza ko ibintu bihagararira aho bigeze, ingabo z'impande zompi zikaguma aho zigeze. Ukraine ivuga ko ivyo bice ikigenzura bihambaye cane ku mutekano wayo muri kazoza.

N'ubwo ata ruhande na rumwe rurerekana ko rwiteguriye kugira ico ruhinduye kuri ivyo, umutegetsi wa Amerika yavuganye n'abamenyeshamakuru ku musi w'imbere y'ibiganiro yavuze ko ivyo ari ivyo izo mpande zerekana ku mugaragaro, ariko ko mu biganiro vyo mw'ibanga, Uburusiya na Ukraine vyerekanye ko hari ivyo vyokwemera guhindura gatoya.

Ariko uwo mutegetsi aremera ko ico kibazo kidashobora gutorerwa umuti hatabayeho ibiganiro ku bijanye n'uburyo bushasha bwagutse bwo gutunganya umutekano inyuma y'intambara.

Yagize ati: "Ntibazoshobora gutorera umuti ikibazo ca Donetsk n'ic'uturere batumvikanako bataramenya ingene uburyo bwo gutunganya umutekano buzoba bumeze inyuma y'intambara".

Yabandanije ati: "Kandi ntimwibagire ko tutazoshobora kwemeza kimwe muri ivyo tutabanje kwumvikana ku kindi."

Ku ruhande rwa Ukraine, ubwo buryo bwo gutunganya umutekano inyuma y'intambara bushobora kuba burimwo ivyemezo vy'uko ibihugu biyishigikiye bizoyitabara ni yongera guterwa.

Ku Burusiya na bwo, hashobora kuba harimwo ico bwamye bwipfuza kuva kera ko ishirahamwe ryo kwivunira umwansi hamwe ry'ibihugu vy'uburengero OTAN (NATO) ryogabanya ibikorwa vyaryo mu bihugu biherereye mu burengero bw'umugabane wa Buraya. Ico ni ikintu gishobora gutera impungenge ibihugu vy'i Buraya.

Mu vyo impande zompi ziriko zirasabwa harimwo ibiganiro hagati yazo ku bibazo vy'umutekano, uburyo bwo guhanahana amakuru bwihuta mu bihe vy'ivyago, hamwe n'ingingo impande zompi zohurizako zo kugabanya umwuka mubi hagati yazo.

Abategetsi ba Amerika bavuga kandi ko hashobora gusubira gushirwaho urwego OTAN n'Uburusiya bihuriramwo, rwari rwahagaritswe ahanini kuva mu 2022.

Ibiganiro biheruka guhuza impande zitatu, vyabereye i Geneve muri Ruhuhuma (2), vyarangiye ata ntambwe ihambaye ishitsweko. Haciye igihe gito, intambara Amerika na Israel vyatanguje kuri Irani yatumye Washington ishira inguvu ahandi maze ntiyasubira kwitaho cane ikibazo ca Ukraine. Kuva ico gihe, nta bindi biganiro vyasubiriye kuba.

Abakuru b'ibihugu vy'i Buraya, ahanini batashizwe mu biganiro bigamije kurangiza iyo ntambara, bagiye basaba ko na bo nyene boba muri vyo. Bahagaritswe umutima n'uko hafatwa ingingo zijanye n'umutekano w'umugabane wabo batabigizemwo uruhara.

Ku wa mbere, umukuru wa Komisiyo y'Ubumwe bw'Uburaya, Ursula von der Leyen, yasavye ko ibihugu bihurikiye muri OTAN hamwe n'ibigize Ubumwe bwa Buraya vyoshirwa mu biganiro vyose bifise aho bihurira n'umutekano w'uyu mugabane.

Perezida Volodymyr Zelensky na we nyene amaze kuvuga incuro zitari nke ko Kyiv ishaka ko umugabane wa Buraya ugira uruhara muri ivyo biganiro.

Umutegetsi wa Amerika yavuze ko Amerika izotanga iciyumviro c'uko ivyo biganiro vyogirwa mu buryo buhuza ibihugu vyinshi, kugira ngo n'umugabane wa Buraya ushirwemwo. Yavuze ati: "Turizigiye ko n'Uburusiya buzovyemera", ariko ashimangira ko "Uburusiya butanezererewe Uburaya".

Kuva atanguye ikiringo ciwe ca kabiri, Perezida wa Amerika Donald Trump - yari yarigeze kwishimagiza avuga ko ashobora kurangiza intambara yo muri Ukraine mu musi umwe - yagiye atunganya ibiganiro bitari bike bigamije kurangiza iyo ntambara, n'ubwo ata kinini vyashitseko.

Hagati aho, ukuntu Trump asa n'uwutera yorohera Moscou vyatumye haba impungenge zikomeye i Kyiv no mu bihugu bigize Ubumwe bwa Buraya.

Inyuma yo guhura na Kirill Dmitriev, intumwa ya Kremlin, i Washington mu ndwi iheze, Trump yavuze ko hagiye kuba "amasezerano akomeye kandi meza cane" yerekeye Ukraine, ashobora "kuba arimwo Uburaya bwose".

Ariko, abantu benshi muri Ukraine ntibemera ko ayo masezerano yoshobora gutuma haboneka amahoro nyayo kandi abereye ku mpande zompi.

Oleksandr Merezhko, umushingamateka wa Ukraine arongoye umurwi ujejwe imigenderanire n'amakungu mu Nama nshingamateka, yabwiye BBC ko abona ko Trump ashaka "amasezerano yihuta, ariko Ukraine ikaba ari yo itanga ikiguzi". Yavuze ko ata nkeka ko Kyiv izoyanka.

Merezhko yavuze ko uburyo bwonyene bwo gutuma Putin atangura ibiganiro vy'ukuri ari ugushira Uburusiya ku gitutu kirushirije, biciye mu bihano no mu kugaba ibitero bikomeye ku bibanza biri kure mu Burusiya.

Yagize ati: "Igihe cose Putin azoba agifise ubushobozi bwo kubandanya intambara, nta mvo n'imwe azoba afise yo kuja mu biganiro".

Yaravuze kandi ko ingingo Trump aheruka gufata, nk'iyerekeye amasezerano yo kugura amazutu mu Burusiya, "ziremesha Moscou zikayiha inguvu zo kubandanya intambara".

Mu ntumwa z'Uburusiya zitaba ibiganiro i Abu Dhabi harimwo Vladimir Medinsky, umujenama mu biro vy'umukuru w'igihugu, ivyegera vy'umushikiranganji w'imigenderanire Sergei Ryabkov na Mikhail Galuzin, Igor Kostyukov arongoye urwego rw'iperereza rwa gisirikare, hamwe n'umusirikare w'ipete rya Jenerale Yury Zhigarlovsky.

Ukraine nayo irungika abategetsi bakuru batari bake bari bagize uruhara mu biganiro vyabaye imbere y'ibi. Muri bo harimwo Rustem Umerov arongoye urwego rw'iperereza ryo hanze y'igihugu, Kyrylo Budanov arongoye ibiro vya Perezida Volodymyr Zelensky, hamwe n'umushingamateka Davyd Arakhamiya.

Mu gihe ivyo biganiro biriko biraba, Uburusiya burabandanya kugaba ibitero bikomeye kandi bihitana abantu muri Ukraine, hamwe no gutera ibingo ntanganguvu. I Kyiv babona ko ivyo ari ikimenyetso c'uko Moscou ishaka gushira Ukraine mu bihe bigoye cane, kugira ngo yemere amasezerano ajanye n'ivyo Uburusiya busaba.

Ku wa mbere, Kushner yakoresheje imvugo yo kwigengesera aho yavuze ko ibiganiro vy'i Abu Dhabi bishobora "gutegura inzira y'iyindi ngunga izokurikira y'ibiganiro".

Yanditse ku rubuga X ati: "Iyi ni intambara igoye cane kandi idasanzwe", yongerako ko Amerika "iriko ija muri ibi biganiro ifise umwete wo kubishikana ku ntumbero, ariko kandi yisunze ibishoboka kandi vy'ukuri".

Iyi gahunda iri mu rwego rwo kuburira abantu bafite ibigo bitaramenyekana cyane, kwirinda abajura cyangwa abariganya bashobora kwiyitirira ibigo by'abandi bakabyambura imitungo cyangwa bakabihombya.

Umuyobozi Mukuru wa RICTA, Grace Ingabire, avuga ko kwandikisha izina ry'ikigo muri RDB bidahagije, ahubwo nyiracyo asabwa no gihita acyandika kuri murandasi kugira ngo hatagira ubona ikirango cyacyo akacyiyitirira, akaba ari we ushyira izina ryacyo kuri murandasi.

Ingabire agira ati "Icyo tubasaba ni ukugira ngo iyo bagiye muri RDB kwandikisha izina ry'ikigo cyabo, be gusoreza aho, ahubwo barenge umutungo wabo mu by'ubwenge, barenge n'ibirango (trademark) byabo, bagere no ku kurinda indangarubuga zabo, na zo bagomba kuba bazifite zandikishijwe".

Ingabire aburira abantu ko iyo umuntu adafite izina ry'ikigo cye kuri murandasi, birangira abandi bantu barimenye, bakarishyira kuri murandasi bagatangira kuricuruza, ariko hakaba n'abigana amazina asanzweho kuri murandasi bakangiza izina ry'ikigo cy'umuntu ku buryo inyungu yari kubona ari bo bayijyanira.

Hari ibyaha byitwa Cybersquatting na phishing bigamije kwigana izina ry'ikigo runaka kizwi, ariko hakaburamo inyuguti, nk'urugero paypal.com ishobora kwitwa paypl.com, aho abakiriya b'icyo kigo batangira kugura ibintu na servisi z'ikindi gishya babonye bacyitiranya n'icyo basanzwe bazi.

Ingabire agira ati "Bigusaba za miliyoni nyinshi z'amafaranga kugira ngo ugarure iryo zina ryawe, cyangwa ukajya mu manza bikaguteza igihombo gikomeye."

Hari n'abandika izina ry'ikigo kizwi ariko bakongeramo inyuguti cyangwa ijambo ryose (urugero nka amazon.com bashobora kongeraho bakavuga ngo amazon.security.com umuntu akaba yagira ngo ni agashami k'icyo kigo), ku buryo iyo bashatse kwiba abantu batangira kubasaba ijambo ry'ibanga ryabo.

Ibi rero ni byo RICTA na RDB baheraho basaba abafite ibigo kugira imbuga(web) zabo z'inyarwanda(zifite izina rya .rw), kugira ngo nibagira ikibazo izo nzego zizabafashe kurenganurwa batitabaje umuntu uri muri Amerika aho bakoresha (.com), cyangwa mu Bufaransa aho bakoresha (.fr). 'Harimo no gukunda igihugu'.

Umukobwa witwa Inema Uwizeye Rita ufite ikigo cyitwa Kira Art Therapy gihangana n'ibibazo by'ubuzima bwo mu mutwe hakoreshejwe ubuhanzi n'ubugeni, avuga ko agomba kwandikisha ikigo cye kuri murandasi kugira ngo batamwiba igitekerezo cye gifitwe na bake ku isi, agahomba igishoro cyose yamaze gushyira mu gushinga icyo kigo.

Dieudonné Irafasha washinze ikigo cyitwa Diolichat cyubaka ikoranabuhanga rya software n'imbuga za murandasi, avuga ko uru rubuga rwigeze kurenza igihe cyo kwishyura indangarubuga ya .rw ruvaho, umuntu uri mu Bushinwa aza gufungura urundi nka rwo, ariko ngo RICTA yamufashije kugarura iryo zina rye no gufunga uwaryiyitiriye uri mu Bushinwa.

Umuyobozi w'Ishami rishinzwe kurengera Umutungo mu by'Ubwenge muri RDB, Blaise Ruhima, avuga ko umuntu washinze ikigo akacyandikisha muri RDB ariko ntiyihutire kugikorera urubuga (cyangwa kurufatira domain name), iyo hagize undi ufata iryo zina bakajyana mu manza, uwashinze ikigo mbere yaho ashobora guhomba ibyo yari yarubatse byose kubera gutakaza izina.

Swans and ducks have enjoyed the wetland reserve at Slimbridge for 80 years

Most people know rainforests are vital in the fight against climate change, but now scientists say wetlands could be even more important.

Saltmarshes, mangrove swamps and wetlands can absorb carbon "four times faster than trees", according to the charity the Wildfowl and Wetlands Trust (WWT).

Celebrating 80 years since WWT's first wetland bird reserve was founded at Slimbridge, in Gloucestershire, the charity's leaders have called for one million hectares of wetlands to be restored across the world.

Sarah Fowler, CEO of WWT, said: "They are mood-boosting, flood-buffering, water-purifying, incredible habitats. But we have lost 85% of the world's wetlands."

Sir Peter Scott feeds migrating swans and geese at Slimbridge in 1947, with Desmond Hawkins, BBC features producer from Bristol

WWT now runs 10 wetland bird reserves across the UK.

Many people come to enjoy the swans, geese, flamingoes and migrating wildfowl, but do not realise how powerful these habitats can be in soaking up carbon and slowing down climate change.

So how vital are wetlands for birds, and how powerful can they be in the fight against climate change?

The swan sanctuary wetland fighting climate change

In November 1946, a naturalist called Peter Scott came to a wild marshy area on the banks of the River Severn, near Slimbridge. He was drawn by the thousands of migrating geese and swans that flew thousands of miles from the Russian Arctic to spend the winter here on the mudflats and marshes.

Captivated, Scott settled in a small cottage and later built a house right on a lake, with a huge window to watch the wildfowl.

He dug lakes and connecting channels, built hides and even towers to watch the birds without disturbing them.

Over the years, the reserve grew and became home to thousands of ducks, swans , geese as well as the migrating wildfowl.

Sir Peter Scott with the first nine Nēnē geese he hand-reared at Slimbridge in 1952

"He really was a pioneer in conservation," said Chris Moore, a historian of Slimbridge and author of Peter Scott and the Birth of Modern Conservation.

As well as creating a safe haven for endangered species, Scott was a vigorous campaigner for nature.

He led the fight to stop commercial whaling, presented some of the BBC's first natural history programmes called live from Slimbridge, and helped set up WWF, the World Wildlife Fund.

In 1973 Sir Peter Scott became the first person to be knighted for conservation work.

Moore explained: "Scott was talking about the impact that man was having on the natural world, long before we started talking about climate change and global warming.

"David Attenborough called him the Patron Saint of Conservation, and I think that is more than deserved," Moore added.

One of Scott's typically ambitious projects was to save the Hawaiian Goose, or Nēnē.

Unique to the Pacific islands, the Nēnē was hit hard by road building and development. By 1949 barely 24 birds remained.

Scott heard of its plight, and asked Hawaiian authorities to send a few geese to Slimbridge where he hand-reared them.

"Unfortunately they sent us two females," chuckled Enid Cole, a WWT volunteer at Slimbridge.

"Peter asked them for a gander - 'It would help', he said."

Nine chicks were later born, and hand-raised successfully to adulthood at Slimbridge.

Dave Harvey helped to feed the Nēnē geese at Slimbridge

Today there are more than 3,000 Nēnē geese, most of them living peacefully on Hawaiian golf courses. But a handful still live at Slimbridge, where Enid Cole and her friends hand feed them lettuce every day.

"It's a marvelous project, and typical of Sir Peter," Enid smiled.

Over the last 80 years, the teams at Slimbridge have hand-reared several other species, including the Common Crane and the world's rarest diving duck, the Madagascan Pochard.

It was while they were working to save the Madagascan Pochard that they realised how vital the wetland habitats were.

"We realised that to save that species, we had to bring the wetland back," explained Sarah Fowler, WWT's chief executive.

"And to bring the wetland back, we had to work with the whole community in Madagascar."

Ian Hollister, a volunteer warden at Slimbridge, said: "The wetlands are great at absorbing carbon, they're like a soggy secret weapon."

Scientists calculate that 85% of the world's wetland habitats have been lost as marshes drained for agriculture, and swamps cleared for construction as cities expand.

And yet, as Fowler explained, "40% of the world's species rely on wetland habitats for survival".

What started at Slimbridge has spread to 10 wetland reserves across the UK with the charity now working with local councils to restore wetlands, even in small city areas.

Wetlands are 'mood-boosting, flood buffering habitats' said Sarah Fowler, Chief Executive of WWT The Wetlands Charity

A scheme in Bristol has seen small floating islands of wetland plants moored in the city's harbour.

Across the world, they are campaigning to restore one million hectares of lost wetland, partly to provide safe habitats for endangered species but also because wetlands help absorb carbon far quicker than even forests.

"Salt marshes bury carbon," said Fowler.

"Every time the big tides go over them, the plants that have grown up in the salt marsh get buried. Those plants are full of carbon, so they are a massive carbon sink.

"And the brilliant thing about salt marshes is they do this four times faster than trees. Wetlands are vital in our fight against climate change, and we must restore them."

What started 80 years ago as a bird reserve on the banks of a river in Gloucestershire has grown into a global campaign to restore wetlands, which they call the "soggy secret weapon" against climate change.
